behavior.arguments: rdx and rsi are pointer arguments. dest = [rdx+8]; q = [[rsi+0x10]+8]; the 16 bytes at q-0x10 are stored at dest; the window returns 1.

edges.copy: dest 0x1000, q 0x2010 -> stores at 0x1000 from source 0x2000, returns 1.
edges.large_address: dest 0xfffffffffffffff0, q 0x1000000000000010 -> stores at 0xfffffffffffffff0 from source 0x1000000000000000, returns 1.
edges.overlapping_region: dest 0x2000, q 0x2010 -> source 0x2000 equals dest; the copy is still the same 16-byte vector move, returns 1.

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with endbr64; straight-line, no branches, no calls: endbr64; mov 0x8(%rdx),%rax; mov 0x10(%rsi),%rdx; mov 0x8(%rdx),%rdx; movdqu -0x10(%rdx),%xmm0; movups %xmm0,(%rax); mov $0x1,%eax; ret.
behavior.return_rule: The return value is the constant 1 in eax, set by mov $0x1,%eax immediately before ret. No condition selects any other return value.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; zero sites found. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: One R_X86_64_RELATIVE record in .rela.dyn names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries). It is reported as a slot list only; no meaning is claimed for the table it belongs to.
